vocabulary.example: The football ticket graph shows cost rising as tickets increase.
vocabulary.visual: Points (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135) climbing left to right — cost by tickets.

copyPanel.rule: Representing Two-Variable Relationships with Tables & Graphs
steps: 1. Construct table: Put independent variable in column 1 (x) and dependent in column 2 (y)
2. Identify the rate of change or rule connecting x to y
3. Plot the ordered pairs on the coordinate plane with x on horizontal axis and y on vertical

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Nakai's Savings Account
revealWordProblem.text:
Nakai opened a savings account with an initial deposit, or principal, of $750. The account earns 3.5% simple interest each year. Interest is the amount paid or earned for the use of the principal, and it is called simple interest when it is figured only on the principal. The graph shows the interest Nakai has earned over time.
Question: What observations can you make about the data using the graph?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A phone screen showing a Main Bank Mobile savings account graph of interest earned in dollars against number of years, with points rising in a straight line from 0 to about 105.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The points lie on a straight line through the origin, so the interest grows at a steady rate — the same amount is added each year. Reading the graph, one year earns about $26, two years about $52, three years about $79, and four years about $105, so each year adds roughly $26. That matches the numbers: 3.5% of $750 is 0.035 × 750 = $26.25 a year. Because the line passes through (0, 0), earning nothing in zero years, the relationship can be written as i = 26.25y, where y is the number of years and i is the interest earned. Extending the line predicts about $131 after 5 years.

questions.stem: Football tickets cost $45 each. What is the total cost of 3 tickets?
questions.explanation: The total cost is 45 times the number of tickets, and 3 × 45 = 135.
choiceFeedback: $45 is the cost of just 1 ticket.
That adds 45 + 3 instead of multiplying 45 × 3.
$90 is the cost of 2 tickets, not 3.
hints: What is the cost of ONE ticket?
Each of the 3 tickets adds another $45.
Multiply the price of one ticket by the number of tickets.
questions.stemEs: Los boletos de fútbol americano cuestan $45 cada uno. ¿Cuál es el costo total de 3 boletos?
questions.explanationEs: El costo total es 45 por el número de boletos, y 3 × 45 = 135.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el costo de UN boleto?
Cada uno de los 3 boletos suma otros $45.
Multiplica el precio de un boleto por el número de boletos.

questions.stem: Which ordered pair belongs on the ticket graph for 2 tickets?
questions.explanation: The number of tickets goes first, and 2 tickets cost 2 × 45 = 90 dollars, so the point is (2, 90).
choiceFeedback: $45 is the cost of 1 ticket, not 2.
That adds 45 + 2 instead of multiplying 45 × 2.
You reversed the coordinates — the independent variable (tickets) goes first.
hints: Which quantity goes first in the ordered pair?
Tickets is the independent variable, so it comes first.
The second number is 2 × 45.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál par ordenado corresponde a 2 boletos en la gráfica de boletos?
questions.explanationEs: El número de boletos va primero, y 2 boletos cuestan 2 × 45 = 90 dólares, así que el punto es (2, 90).
hintsEs: ¿Cuál cantidad va primero en el par ordenado?
Los boletos son la variable independiente, así que van primero.
El segundo número es 2 × 45.

questions.stem: On the ticket graph, what should the two axes be labeled?
choices: Number of tickets and price of one ticket
Number of tickets and total cost
Number of games and number of tickets
questions.explanation: Each axis is labeled with one quantity from the problem — one axis shows the number of tickets and the other shows the total cost.
choiceFeedback: The price of one ticket is fixed at $45 — it is not a changing quantity, so it does not get an axis.
$45 is a fixed rate, not a variable quantity that gets its own axis.
The number of games is not one of the two quantities in this problem.
hints: Which TWO quantities change in this situation?
One is the choice; the other responds to it.
You choose the tickets, and the total cost responds.
questions.stemEs: En la gráfica de boletos, ¿cómo se deben rotular los dos ejes?
questions.explanationEs: Cada eje se rotula con una cantidad del problema — un eje muestra el número de boletos y el otro muestra el costo total.
hintsEs: ¿Cuáles DOS cantidades cambian en esta situación?
Uno es lo que se escoge; el otro responde a eso.
Tú escoges los boletos, y el costo total responde.

level1.stem: The Sandia Peak tram travels 1,200 feet each minute. How far has it traveled after 3 minutes?
level1.explanation: The tram covers 1,200 feet every minute, so after 3 minutes it has gone 3 × 1,200 = 3,600 feet.
choiceFeedback: 1,200 feet is the distance after only 1 minute.
That adds 1,200 + 3 instead of multiplying 1,200 × 3.
2,400 feet is the distance after 2 minutes, not 3.
hints: How far does the tram go in ONE minute?
Each minute adds another 1,200 feet.
Multiply 1,200 by the number of minutes.
level1.stemEs: El tranvía de Sandia Peak recorre 1,200 pies por minuto. ¿Qué distancia ha recorrido después de 3 minutos?
level1.explanationEs: El tranvía recorre 1,200 pies cada minuto, así que después de 3 minutos ha avanzado 3 × 1,200 = 3,600 pies.
hintsEs: ¿Qué distancia recorre el tranvía en UN minuto?
Cada minuto suma otros 1,200 pies.
Multiplica 1,200 por el número de minutos.

level1.stem: A table shows a train traveling 48 kilometers every hour: 1 hour, 48 km; 5 hours, 240 km. How many kilometers does it travel in 2 hours?
level1.explanation: At 48 kilometers per hour, 2 hours gives 2 × 48 = 96 kilometers.
choiceFeedback: 48 km is the distance for 1 hour, not 2.
That adds 48 + 2 instead of multiplying 48 × 2.
144 km is the distance for 3 hours, not 2.
hints: How far in ONE hour?
Each hour adds another 48 km.
Multiply 48 by 2.
level1.stemEs: Una tabla muestra un tren que viaja 48 kilómetros cada hora: 1 hora, 48 km; 5 horas, 240 km. ¿Cuántos kilómetros viaja en 2 horas?
level1.explanationEs: A 48 kilómetros por hora, 2 horas dan 2 × 48 = 96 kilómetros.
hintsEs: ¿Qué distancia en UNA hora?
Cada hora suma otros 48 km.
Multiplica 48 por 2.

level1.stem: As the number of tickets purchased increases, the total cost…
level1.explanation: Every extra ticket adds another $45, so the total cost rises as the number of tickets rises.
choiceFeedback: Buying MORE tickets cannot make the total go down — each ticket adds $45.
The table shows different totals ($45, $90, $135), so the cost does not stay the same.
The relationship is clear from the table: more tickets always means a higher total.
hints: Compare the totals for 1, 2, and 3 tickets.
$45, $90, $135 — which direction is that going?
Each new ticket adds to the total.
level1.stemEs: Conforme aumenta el número de boletos comprados, el costo total…
level1.explanationEs: Cada boleto adicional suma otros $45, así que el costo total sube conforme sube el número de boletos.
hintsEs: Compara los totales de 1, 2 y 3 boletos.
$45, $90, $135 — ¿en qué dirección va eso?
Cada boleto nuevo se suma al total.

level2.stem: The Sandia Peak tram travels 1,200 feet each minute and the ascent takes 15 minutes. How long is the whole ascent in feet?
choiceFeedback: That adds 1,200 + 15 instead of multiplying 1,200 × 15.
12,000 feet is the distance after 10 minutes, not the full 15.
16,800 feet is the distance after 14 minutes — one minute short of the top.
hints: How many minutes does the full ascent take?
Each of those 15 minutes covers 1,200 feet.
Multiply 1,200 by 15.
level2.stemEs: El tranvía de Sandia Peak recorre 1,200 pies por minuto y el ascenso toma 15 minutos. ¿Cuánto mide todo el ascenso en pies?
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos minutos toma todo el ascenso?
Cada uno de esos 15 minutos cubre 1,200 pies.
Multiplica 1,200 por 15.

level2.stem: On the tram graph with minutes on the horizontal axis and feet on the vertical axis, which ordered pair lies on the graph?
level2.explanation: After 5 minutes the tram has traveled 5 × 1,200 = 6,000 feet, so the point is (5, 6000).
choiceFeedback: 1,200 feet is the distance for 1 minute, not 5.
5,000 rounds the rate to 1,000 feet per minute — the tram travels 1,200 feet each minute.
You reversed the coordinates — time (the independent variable) goes first.
hints: Which axis is time on?
The second coordinate is the distance after 5 minutes.
Multiply 5 by 1,200.
level2.stemEs: En la gráfica del tranvía con los minutos en el eje horizontal y los pies en el eje vertical, ¿cuál par ordenado está en la gráfica?
level2.explanationEs: Después de 5 minutos el tranvía ha recorrido 5 × 1,200 = 6,000 pies, así que el punto es (5, 6000).
hintsEs: ¿En cuál eje va el tiempo?
La segunda coordenada es la distancia después de 5 minutos.
Multiplica 5 por 1,200.

level2.stem: A table pairs hours with kilometers: (1, 48), (2, 96), (5, 240). How many kilometers are traveled each hour?
level2.explanation: Each row is 48 times the number of hours: 2 × 48 = 96 and 5 × 48 = 240, so the rate is 48 kilometers per hour.
choiceFeedback: 24 splits the first rate in half, but the table shows a different distance in that very first hour.
96 km is the distance for 2 hours — divide it by 2 to get the rate for 1 hour.
240 km is the distance for 5 hours, not the per-hour rate.
hints: Look at the row for 1 hour.
Check it with another row: does 2 hours give twice as much?
The rate is the distance for exactly one hour.
level2.stemEs: Una tabla relaciona horas con kilómetros: (1, 48), (2, 96), (5, 240). ¿Cuántos kilómetros se recorren cada hora?
level2.explanationEs: Cada fila es 48 por el número de horas: 2 × 48 = 96 y 5 × 48 = 240, así que la tasa es 48 kilómetros por hora.
hintsEs: Mira la fila de 1 hora.
Compruébalo con otra fila: ¿2 horas dan el doble?
La tasa es la distancia de exactamente una hora.

level2.stem: Why is the line on the football ticket graph dashed instead of solid?
choices: Dashed lines always mean the cost is decreasing
The ticket price changes between points
You can only buy whole numbers of tickets, so the points between whole numbers do not make sense
level2.explanation: You cannot buy 2.5 tickets, so only the whole-number points represent real purchases — the dashes show the trend without claiming the in-between points are possible.
choiceFeedback: The graph is complete — the dashes are a deliberate choice about what the in-between values mean.
Dashes say nothing about direction; this cost is increasing.
The price stays $45 per ticket everywhere on the graph.
hints: Could you buy half a ticket?
Which points on the line represent real purchases?
Only whole numbers of tickets make sense here.
level2.stemEs: ¿Por qué la línea de la gráfica de boletos de fútbol americano es punteada en vez de continua?
level2.explanationEs: No puedes comprar 2.5 boletos, así que solo los puntos con números enteros representan compras reales — las líneas punteadas muestran la tendencia sin afirmar que los puntos intermedios sean posibles.
hintsEs: ¿Podrías comprar medio boleto?
¿Cuáles puntos de la línea representan compras reales?
Aquí solo tienen sentido los números enteros de boletos.

level2.stem: The ticket table and ticket graph are two representations. Which statement about them is true?
choices: The graph shows a different relationship than the table
Only the table can show that cost increases with tickets
Only the graph is a real mathematical representation
Both show the same relationship — the table with numerical values, the graph in a more visual way
level2.explanation: Every row of the table is plotted as a point, so both show cost = 45 × tickets — the table numerically, the graph visually.
choiceFeedback: Each point on the graph comes straight from a row of the table — they show the SAME relationship.
The graph also shows the increase: the points rise to the right.
Tables are just as mathematical as graphs — they show the same pairs of values.
hints: Where do the graph's points come from?
Each table row becomes one point.
Same pairs, two different pictures.
level2.stemEs: La tabla de boletos y la gráfica de boletos son dos representaciones. ¿Cuál enunciado sobre ellas es verdadero?
level2.explanationEs: Cada fila de la tabla se ubica como un punto, así que ambos muestran costo = 45 × boletos — la tabla de forma numérica, la gráfica de forma visual.
hintsEs: ¿De dónde vienen los puntos de la gráfica?
Cada fila de la tabla se convierte en un punto.
Los mismos pares, dos dibujos distintos.

level3.stem: A stadium shuttle carries fans from the parking lot. The table pairs the number of trips with the total fans carried: 2 trips with 96 fans, 5 trips with 240 fans, and 8 trips with 384 fans. On a graph with trips on the horizontal axis and fans on the vertical axis, which ordered pair belongs to 3 trips?
choiceFeedback: 51 is not three times the rate. Every row runs 48 fans per trip, so three trips carry three times 48.
48 is the number of fans for ONE trip. Three trips carry three times that.
The coordinates are swapped. Trips is the horizontal coordinate and fans the vertical.
level3.explanation: Every row of the table is 48 times the number of trips: 96 ÷ 2 = 48, 240 ÷ 5 = 48, and 384 ÷ 8 = 48. The independent variable, trips, is written first, and 3 × 48 = 144, so the ordered pair is (3, 144).

level3.stem: Nakai's savings account has a principal of $750 and earns 3.5% simple interest each year. How much interest does Nakai earn in one year?
level3.explanation: One year of interest is 3.5% of $750: 0.035 × 750 = 26.25.
choiceFeedback: That treats 3.5% as $3.50 flat instead of taking 3.5% OF the $750 principal.
That is 10% of $750, not 3.5%.
That is 35% of $750 — the decimal point for 3.5% is one place further left.
hints: Write 3.5% as a decimal.
Multiply 0.035 by 750.
level3.stemEs: La cuenta de ahorros de Nakai tiene un capital de $750 y gana 3.5% de interés simple al año. ¿Cuánto interés gana Nakai en un año?
level3.explanationEs: Un año de interés es 3.5% de $750: 0.035 × 750 = 26.25.
hintsEs: Escribe 3.5% como decimal.
Multiplica 0.035 por 750.

level3.stem: Nakai earns $26.25 in simple interest every year. On the graph of years vs. interest earned, which point represents 4 years?
level3.explanation: After 4 years the interest earned is 4 × 26.25 = 105 dollars, so the point is (4, 105).
choiceFeedback: $26.25 is the interest for 1 year, not 4.
$78.75 is the interest after 3 years — one year short.
$750 is the principal Nakai deposited, not interest earned.
hints: How much interest arrives EACH year?
Four years means four equal payments of $26.25.
Multiply 26.25 by 4.
level3.stemEs: Nakai gana $26.25 de interés simple cada año. En la gráfica de años vs. interés ganado, ¿cuál punto representa 4 años?
level3.explanationEs: Después de 4 años el interés ganado es 4 × 26.25 = 105 dólares, así que el punto es (4, 105).
hintsEs: ¿Cuánto interés llega CADA año?
Cuatro años significan cuatro pagos iguales de $26.25.
Multiplica 26.25 por 4.

level3.stem: After 10 minutes, the Sandia Peak tram has traveled 12,000 feet. The whole ascent is 18,000 feet. How much farther must it travel to reach the top?
level3.explanation: The remaining distance is 18,000 − 12,000 = 6,000 feet — which matches the last 5 minutes at 1,200 feet per minute.
choiceFeedback: 1,200 feet is only one more minute of travel — 5 minutes remain.
Check with the rate: 5 remaining minutes × 1,200 feet is 6,000, not 5,000.
12,000 feet is the distance already traveled, not what remains.
hints: How is 'distance remaining' related to the total?
Subtract the distance traveled from 18,000.
Check your answer: 5 minutes remain at 1,200 feet per minute.
level3.stemEs: Después de 10 minutos, el tranvía de Sandia Peak ha recorrido 12,000 pies. Todo el ascenso son 18,000 pies. ¿Cuánto más debe recorrer para llegar a la cima?
level3.explanationEs: La distancia que falta es 18,000 − 12,000 = 6,000 pies — que coincide con los últimos 5 minutos a 1,200 pies por minuto.
hintsEs: ¿Cómo se relaciona la 'distancia que falta' con el total?
Resta la distancia recorrida de 18,000.
Revisa tu respuesta: quedan 5 minutos a 1,200 pies por minuto.

level3.stem: A second tram travels 900 feet per minute. If both trams are graphed on the same axes (minutes vs. feet), how do the graphs compare?
choices: The 900 ft/min line rises more steeply
The Sandia Peak line (1,200 ft/min) rises more steeply than the 900 ft/min line
level3.explanation: In one minute, the Sandia tram climbs 1,200 feet on the graph while the other climbs only 900 — a faster rate makes a steeper line.
choiceFeedback: Steepness follows the rate: 900 feet per minute rises LESS each minute than 1,200.
Different rates give different points — at 1 minute one graph is at 900 and the other at 1,200.
Both trams gain distance over time, so both lines rise.
hints: Compare where each graph is after 1 minute.
One is at 900 feet, the other at 1,200 feet.
The faster rate climbs more per minute — steeper.
level3.stemEs: Un segundo tranvía viaja 900 pies por minuto. Si ambos tranvías se grafican en los mismos ejes (minutos vs. pies), ¿cómo se comparan las gráficas?
level3.explanationEs: En un minuto, el tranvía de Sandia sube 1,200 pies en la gráfica mientras que el otro sube solo 900 — una tasa más rápida hace una línea más empinada.
hintsEs: Compara dónde está cada gráfica después de 1 minuto.
Uno está en 900 pies, el otro en 1,200 pies.
La tasa más rápida sube más por minuto — más empinada.

predict.stem: Before you build the table — each ticket costs $45. Which ordered pair shows 3 tickets?
predict.explanation: The number of tickets is the independent variable, so it goes first: 3 tickets cost 3 × $45 = $135, giving (3, 135).
choiceFeedback: That reverses the coordinates, writing (cost, tickets). The independent variable always comes FIRST.
That keeps the cost of one ticket instead of the cost of 3.
That puts the price first. Tickets are the independent variable, so tickets lead.
